content_html:
How Memories Are Stored and Reconstructed

Memories are stored as durable, distributed traces (changes in synapses, spines, and molecular states) across neural networks. At recall, partial cues trigger reconstruction by reactivating these engram circuits, often with the hippocampus coordinating pattern completion and the neocortex providing distributed content.

This flow emphasizes durable storage traces (synapses, spines, molecular marks) that support later reconstruction by engram circuits.

Key Evidence & Concepts

  • Synaptic plasticity as storage: Long-term potentiation/depression and spine remodeling provide durable changes after learning.
  • Engrams: Ensembles of neurons causally linked to a specific memory; optogenetic activation can drive recall of tagged memories in mice.
  • Systems consolidation: Hippocampus rapidly encodes; over time and with sleep replay, neocortical traces strengthen.
  • Reconstruction & attractors: Recurrent circuits support pattern completion; recall is constructive and can be distorted.
  • Lesion dissociations: Hippocampal damage impairs new episodic memory (H.M.), while older consolidated memories are relatively spared.
